concept.name: Municipal SLA & Service Bottleneck Operations Explorer
concept.targetBuyer: Municipal operations managers, public works team leads, or service contractors
concept.buyerProblem: Public 311 exports can omit the target and closure timestamps needed for SLA review, so operations teams need an explicit adapter boundary and a safe way to evaluate authorized enriched records without treating missing fields as evidence.
concept.centralClaim: Given an explicitly synthetic, adapter-ready service-request fixture with created, target, and closure timestamps, the engine can reproducibly calculate scenario margins, route malformed inputs to review, aggregate ward scenarios, and export auditable results without claiming official municipal performance.

authorizedScope: Human approved the web UI, visual 3-page PDF, Project Manifest, independent validation, Vercel hosting, GitHub release, and Upwork portfolio publication on 2026-09-08. Paid services, live municipal dispatch integration, and legal SLA certifications remain unauthorized.
nextAction: WS-003 is released. Preserve this final state and immutable evidence. Begin no WS-004 work until fresh scope and publication approval are recorded.

humanApproval.basis: The user approved publication on 2026-09-08, the four-finding remediation on 2026-09-12, and resumption of the independent validator after its runtime interruption on 2026-09-12.

limitations: No client posting was supplied; demand evidence is based on general operational dashboard and monitoring signals.
The proof uses 15 synthetic 311-style records; it is not a recorded Toronto extract and does not estimate production accuracy.
Toronto's current public 311 export does not expose target or closure timestamps, so production calculations require an authorized internal adapter.
The scenario calculations do not constitute official municipal performance metrics, staffing instructions, dispatch commands, or legal certifications.

release.upworkPortfolioTitle: Municipal 311 SLA Operations Desk | Response Analytics & Ward Bottlenecks
release.upworkPublicationEvidence: User confirmed item number 3 is published on 2026-09-12; current listing copy and attachment were not reverified because browser control was unavailable.

lessons: Validate source columns before framing timing claims; licensed context does not supply missing target or closure evidence.
Treat lifecycle consistency and complete origin equality as release-critical adversarial cases, not optional hardening.
Keep mutable portfolio status out of shared files hash-locked by prior releases; use the tracking catalog unless older evidence is independently recertified.
A builder-side pass cannot replace the fresh non-builder report or executable hash gate.
